- We've seen the same error spike in telemetry for your customer id (KF-45).
- No model rollout on your default route in the last 3 hours per control-plane audit.
- Preliminary signal: memory pressure on the rerank worker causing KV cache evictions and a cascading retry storm.

Subject: Internal: Kingfisher — rapid mitigation plan (do not forward)

Team — quick coordination note (internal):

Telemetry snapshot (08:40–09:30 PDT):
- Aggregate 5xx rate: 6.1% (baseline 0.3%)
- p50/p95 token latency: 280ms / 1.82s (baseline 220ms / 900ms)
- Error class: OOM-like worker crashes and connection timeouts at the rerank layer

Immediate mitigations in-flight:
- Traffic split: route 30% -> quantized-compact (lower memory footprint).
- Warmed cold caches for hot prefixes for the rerank model; primed KV on idle replicas.
- Increased soft-concurrency limits on Dedicated pool KF-45 by +25%.
- Short-lived request-level retries capped to 0 to avoid retry amplification.

What we need from each owner:
- Monica: prepare a 11:00 exec slide with one-liner impact + ETA to full restoration.
- Laura: draft customer-facing language for the 11:00 update and for Sarah Patel (VP).
- David: capture runtime traces and a sample flame graph — paste to the incident.
- Karthik: ensure autoscaler hasn't flapped; if so, hold scale-downs for 30m.

If these mitigations do not reduce error rate within 20 minutes, we will consider a temporary downgrade of the rerank model cache policy and extend the traffic diversion.

— Priyom

Quick executive note ahead of the 11:00 call. Please find the short status below and a clear set of next steps we will present.

One-line status: We have identified memory pressure on the rerank worker leading to cache evictions and elevated 5xx; mitigations have been applied and we're monitoring for improvement.

Impact: ~6% of API calls for the rerank endpoint experienced errors between 08:45–09:20 PDT; some requests may have received delayed responses impacting checkout personalization.

Immediate next steps (we will deliver these on the 11:00 call):
- Stabilization: maintain 30% traffic on quantized-compact variant for 30 minutes and keep concurrency bumped until telemetry recovers.
- Validation: run a deterministic scoring comparison across a 100k sample to confirm parity — results expected by 13:00 PDT.
- Remediation: if instability persists after 30 minutes, we will temporarily change cache policy and extend diversion; we will coordinate rollback plans for any revenue-sensitive jobs.
- Credits: if SLA thresholds are breached, we'll work with your finance team; we will provide an initial credit estimate within 24 hours.

We will keep the post-incident root cause analysis and timeline transparent — Priyom will follow up with artifact links.

Subject: Post-incident: Kingfisher — stabilization complete & next steps (KF-3241)

Team / Olivia — final update on KF-3241.

Summary: At ~09:40 PDT on Sep 25 we observed steady recovery after the traffic split and increased concurrency; by 10:20 PDT error rate returned to baseline (<0.5%) and p95 latency to normal ranges. The immediate customer impact window was ~35 minutes.

Root cause (initial): A regression in the rerank model's in-memory index size combined with a recent cache TTL change led to excessive KV evictions under burst load. The model itself did not receive a new deployment; the index growth was due to a data drift scenario that increased hot-prefix diversity.

Actions taken:
- Immediate: traffic diversion (quantized-compact), concurrency bump, cache priming.
- Short-term: reverted the cache TTL change and applied a safety cap on in-memory index growth.
- Long-term: added telemetry for index cardinality, an early-warning on cache eviction spike, and a workflow to run deterministic parity checks before any cache/TTL changes.

Customer-facing follow-ups we committed to:
1) A deterministic scoring comparison (results uploaded to shared drive) by 13:00 PDT 9/25 — attached link.
2) A credit estimate and formal SLA review within 24 hours.
3) Post-mortem with timeline, root cause, and remediation items in 72 hours.

I've opened a postmortem ticket (KF-3241) and drafted the PM template: postmortem-ticket-KF-3241.md. Please add blockers or ops notes to the Jira.

Thanks to the on-call and infra teams for the quick response.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
